display_title_he: ביקורת על המשחק Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse
short_summary: Evil Empire and Konami return with Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse, blending Dead Cells-inspired mechanics with classic gothic action.

sources.name: Polygon
sources.title: Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse Is a Near-Perfect Metroidvania

paragraphs: After more than a decade away from the spotlight, the legendary Castlevania franchise returns with Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse, developed by Evil Empire. Fans who fondly remember earlier installments can now look forward to a modern revival that successfully balances throwback appeal with fresh gameplay mechanics, proving the series still has plenty to offer alongside spiritual successors like Bloodstained: Ritual of the Night.

The narrative picks up nearly two decades after Trevor Belmont and his allies defeated Dracula. Players step into the shoes of Rose Belmont, a relatively fresh-faced vampire hunter and the daughter of Sypha Belnades and Trevor. Prompted by a warning letter received by her father, Rose travels to Paris to investigate dark phenomena. Before long, she finds herself separated and facing the forces of hell, as well as an emotional curse tied to her feelings that threatens her future.

Visually, the game opts for hyperstylized 2.5D graphics, turning the once-lively city of Paris into a striking ghost town filled with dramatic reds and oranges against a backdrop of rotting corpses. The open-world environment offers plenty of room for discovery, featuring substantive secrets, hidden puzzles, and branching paths. Unlike some sprawling adventures, it avoids frustrating exploration loops by keeping the main path clear and rewarding.

One of the most notable additions is the Arcana system, a collection of magical tarot cards inherited from Rose's mother. Players unlock these cards by defeating powerful bosses or assisting transformed souls, turning former foes into friends. These cards grant satisfying powers that expend mana, allowing Rose to shoot fireballs, freeze enemies, or manipulate time. This system ties into the storytelling, touching on themes of redemption and forgiveness as Rose confronts wretched beings.

Combat builds upon the ultra-responsive controls of Dead Cells. Instead of relying on traditional invincible evasion frames, players must carefully read enemy movements, slide, backstep, jump, and parry incoming attacks using a magic whip or a rewarding defensive parry. Upgrades allow players to zoom across the map using movement tricks and cancels, enhancing both monster duels and platforming.

While the game features minor flaws—such as the absence of quick-swapping for weapons and magic, which requires players to pause and leaf through menus, and simplified weapon upgrade tiers—the overall experience remains exceptionally polished, atmospheric, and engaging.

Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse launches on October 15 across Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, and Xbox Series X, accompanied by a pulsing musical score that features the tune "Bloody Tears."

facts.fact: Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse is developed by Evil Empire and published by Konami, marking the first mainline installment in the series in over a decade.
The game stars Rose Belmont, the daughter of Trevor Belmont and Sypha Belnades, who investigates dark happenings in Paris alongside her father.
Gameplay combines Dead Cells-inspired responsive controls with a new card-based Arcana system and 2.5D gothic visuals.
The title is scheduled for release on October 15 across Nintendo Switch, Nintendo Switch 2, PlayStation 5, Windows PC, and Xbox Series X.
